clue.text: A lounge prepared for 13 on the May the first

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up from raw materials, so the letters are made over into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone readies a lounge for a visitor arriving on May Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN, the poets' theme: Maya Angelou, whose first name is May followed by the first letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Maya Angelou was a celebrated American poet and memoirist, and her forename is MAY plus the first letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Late Tertiary personality turning up in East Anglian river

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, which wraps round it

parts.note: the Nene flows through Northamptonshire and the Fens to the Wash

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the ego is the self or personality

explanation.surface: Someone from late prehistoric times surfaces in a Norfolk river.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed self-image is split round the middle of the river's name, not just placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neogene is the geological period forming the later part of what was formerly called the Tertiary era.

clue.text: Singular communist editor of Wisden

indicators.note: the name ends like a plural, so making it singular drops its final letter

parts.note: Friedrich Engels, co-author of the Communist Manifesto

explanation.surface: A cricket almanac's editor is oddly described as a one-of-a-kind communist.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisden is the annual cricket almanac; Matthew Engel edited it from 1993. Engels loses his S as though it were a plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Engel, a Guardian journalist, served as editor of Wisden Cricketers' Almanack in the 1990s and 2000s.

clue.text: When it breaks out, endless weaponry will be used…

definitions.text: When it breaks out, endless weaponry will be used…

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter
breaking out suggests an eruption that scatters the letters into disorder

parts.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A warning that once hostilities start, arms will be deployed without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition, and it runs on into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Open war is undisguised, full-scale conflict, exactly the situation in which every weapon gets used.

clue.text: Observed the end of Man — out of the wood?

parts.note: past tense of see
dust to dust: mankind ends as dust, as the burial service says

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed the death of mankind and asks whether we are safe now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the wood' suggests escaping danger; read literally, it is the powder that comes from cut timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawdust is the fine powder produced when timber is cut, literally material coming out of wood.

clue.text: …by the military, with a sign about their leader

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sign wraps around the other letter

parts.note: Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac
their refers back to the military, whose leading letter this is

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 down: weapons used by soldiers, who rally round their commander's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 4 down. 'Their leader' is the first letter of military, the word just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies are a nation's organised land forces, so the plural noun stands for the military as a body.

clue.text: Emily the 13 in the back yard like a child?

indicators.note: the back says this word is placed at the rear, after the other piece

parts.note: both are old slang for the penis
taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: The poet Emily pictured playing outside in the garden like a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN. 'In the back yard' puts IN at the back of the slang word, and a child follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was a reclusive nineteenth-century American poet from Amherst, Massachusetts.

clue.text: Having taken a chair, I had a meal which will be enough for me

definitions.note: the clue's verb phrase; satiate means to fill or satisfy completely

parts.note: sat down on a chair
taken as written
ate is had a meal

explanation.surface: A diner sits down, eats and declares it will do nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate someone is to supply them fully, giving them as much food as they could want.

clue.text: Inside most of the land between sea and river is 13

indicators.note: split as in side, this places the central chain within a word for a side
most of means the word loses a letter, here its last
between places this piece in the middle, with one on either side

parts.note: a side is an edge; its letters open and close the answer
the Aral Sea in Central Asia
taken as written
the Po is Italy's longest river
the last letter of the word for side, closing it round the chain

explanation.surface: A puzzling geography: some territory between sea and river is somehow American.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Inside' as 'in side': the chain of sea, shortened land and river goes into a word for side, just before its final letter. 13 is AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet and short-story writer, author of The Raven.

clue.text: 13 a tall guy?
Prevalence in half French town?

parts.note: the French words for in and half are en and demi
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Wondering whether something is common in one half of a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks as if it qualifies the town, but it translates the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemicity is the state of a disease being regularly present in an area, its prevalence there.

clue.text: See 10

parts.note: surface reading: an ordinary cross-reference with no wordplay of its own
setter's reading: look at 10 across, whose clue ends with guy, which this light means

explanation.walkthrough: This is the second half of the poet in 10 across, LONG + FELLOW; the 'guy' of that clue defines this half.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is an informal word for a man or chap, the same as the guy named in the other clue.

clue.text: Camera in operation 14 from where we are

indicators.note: something in operation is being worked, so the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also belongs to the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A camera is running, filming something western as seen from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty: it is part of the letters to be rearranged as well as of the indicator phrase. 14 is HESPERIAN, western.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, where the setter writes, the United States lies to the west, so its people are westerners.

clue.text: Western men with fairy article

parts.note: jocular plural of he: males
a peri is a fairy of Persian legend
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cowboys accompanied by a story-book creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' tempts as a film genre with men in it; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperian is a literary word meaning of the west, from Hesperus, the evening star.

clue.text: Attitudiniser after Geller''s model

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar
Uri Geller, the spoon-bending showman
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A poser imitating the style of Uri Geller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an exemplar to follow; it is the Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitudiniser strikes poses for effect, and a posturist is likewise one who adopts affected postures.

clue.text: A fall guy (9) with a 13 girl

parts.note: the thematic 13 is American, abbreviated as for the country
a pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A stuntman who takes tumbles teams up with a girl from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall guy' suggests a scapegoat, but (9) points to 9 down: Roderick Usher of Poe's The Fall of the House of Usher.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderick Usher is the doomed central figure in Poe's tale The Fall of the House of Usher.

clue.text: Disappointing weather for 13
Give food and drink to one making decisions about silence

parts.note: a referee makes decisions in a game
re means concerning
the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Offering a snack to a judge who rules on keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh someone is to restore them with something to eat or drink, as in light refreshments.

clue.text: Proximity causing many to lose head

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
taken as written
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Being too close together makes lots of people panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose head' reads as panic, but head is a headland here.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness and proximity are synonyms, both meaning nearness in space or relationship.

clue.text: Mozart's associate to go to bed in a dress

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the garment

parts.note: a sari is a draped Indian dress
lie down to sleep

explanation.surface: Someone close to Mozart retires for the night still wearing a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri was a court composer in Vienna, Mozart's contemporary and supposed rival.

clue.text: Spend, spend, spend — rise of record-breaking powerful increase

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a surge is a powerful rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise reads the word from the bottom up

parts.note: a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A spending spree described as a record-breaking boom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend, spend, spend' was the famous cry of pools winner Viv Nicholson.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend money lavishly and extravagantly, as the repeated command suggests.

clue.text: Rattles damaged stairs

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters fall into another order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A broken staircase creaks and clatters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sistra, plural of sistrum, are ancient Egyptian metal percussion instruments shaken to make a jingling noise.

clue.text: Gush of these nine13s, perhaps, turned off in use

indicators.note: turned means the letters are spun round into a new arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A flood of verse from the nine American poets, switched off once in use.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine 13s are the thematic American poets in the grid; their poems might be called effusions.
explanation.definitionFit: An effusion is an unrestrained outpouring of words or feeling, and the term is used of gushing verse.

clue.text: See clearly — 13

parts.note: lo means look or see
to see well is to see clearly

explanation.surface: A short instruction to look carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Lowell and Amy Lowell were both American poets of the twentieth century.

clue.text: 14 temperature for grain

parts.note: 14 is the word meaning western, and W is its abbreviation
heat is a level of temperature

explanation.surface: How hot it should be in the west for growing cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is the cereal grass whose seed is the grain ground for flour.

clue.text: High wire holds 13 flower

indicators.note: holds means the outer pieces grip the other one inside them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for high
T. S. Eliot, the American-born poet
wire rope; a wire is a cord like a rope

explanation.surface: A tightrope stretched up high supports a poet among the blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High wire' looks like a circus act; the two words supply the outer letters separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliotrope is a garden plant with fragrant purple flowers that turn towards the sun.

clue.text: Pound of the 13 bible

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the forename of an American poet surnamed Pound
second meaning: a book of the Old Testament

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money or a weight; it is the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was a modernist American poet, and Ezra is also a book in the Old Testament scriptures.

clue.text: Caucasian male dropping English 13

indicators.note: dropping means letting a letter fall out of the phrase

parts.note: a Caucasian is a white person
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A white man giving up his English nationality to become American.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Walt Whitman, author of Leaves of Grass, is among the best-known nineteenth-century American poets.

clue.text: 13 may be said to be more amusing

indicators.note: may be said points to how the name is pronounced rather than written

parts.note: John Greenleaf Whittier, the American poet

explanation.surface: An American is said to be funnier.
explanation.walkthrough: In most accents the H of the poet's name is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative adjective: wittier means showing more humour and cleverness, hence funnier.
